claims.head: Bruisers against finesse
claims.body: The Flyers hit a lot, but the Sabres mostly don’t. Philadelphia is one of the league’s best for physicality, and Buffalo is near the bottom. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Flyers.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 21% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Owen Tippett is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward.
Tyson Foerster is day to day (hand injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Cam York is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Nick Seeler has taken his spot beside Jamie Drysdale.
Travis Konecny is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-six forward.

BUF.head: The Sabres should have the upper hand
BUF.body: Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, gets Dahlin back and has home-ice advantage. The Flyers can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.

PHI.head: The Flyers face a real test
PHI.body: Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, gets Dahlin back and has home-ice advantage. The Flyers’ best way through is a penalty kill that holds up.
